topic: Teleport Beams LLM Proxy: Delegated Identity for Production AI Agents

summary.what: Teleport launched Beams public beta on June 16, 2026, introducing two foundational capabilities of its Agentic Identity Framework: LLM Proxy and Delegated Identity. These solve the critical gap of identity, access control, and audit for AI agents at the two most consequential points in agentic workflows — what the agent is instructed to do (LLM Proxy) and what it is permitted to access (Delegated Identity).
summary.whyNow: 69% of infrastructure leaders say widespread AI adoption requires significant changes to identity management. Only 18% of security leaders are highly confident their current IAM can manage agent identities. 55% cite sensitive data exposure as top concern. 40% increasing identity/security budgets for AI agent risks.
summary.keyInnovation: Beams runs each agent in an isolated Firecracker VM with built-in Teleport-issued identity — no secrets, no static API keys, full audit from instantiation to termination. The LLM Proxy sits between agent and inference endpoint, inspecting every request/response and writing to audit log. Delegated Identity allows scoped, ephemeral permissions per task — least-privilege as a runtime property.

competitorLandscape.name: Okta
competitorLandscape.angle: Zero Trust for machines / AI agent identities
competitorLandscape.keyContent: Okta published 'Zero Trust for machines: Securing AI agent identities' (May 20, 2026) — focuses on stopping use of static keys, securing agents with Okta and Model Context Protocol (MCP). Positioned as identity-as-a-service for agentic workflows.
competitorLandscape.differentiation: Broader IAM platform play, not purpose-built for agent runtimes. No isolated VM-based agent execution environment.

competitorLandscape.name: Strata Identity (now Rubrik)
competitorLandscape.keyContent: Commissioned CSA survey (285 IT/security pros) showing: only 18% confident in current IAM for agents; 44% use static API keys; 28% can trace agent actions to human. Position Maverics as 'AI Identity Gateway' for policy enforcement via OBO token exchange.
competitorLandscape.differentiation: Focused on identity orchestration layer, not runtime isolation. No agent execution environment.

competitorLandscape.name: CyberArk
competitorLandscape.keyContent: Research showing 91% of privileged access is always-on. Pushing JIT access for zero trust. Focused on credential vaulting and standing privilege reduction.
competitorLandscape.differentiation: Traditional PAM approach — credentials/secrets focus, not agent-native identity model.

competitorLandscape.name: Zentera Systems
competitorLandscape.angle: Zero Trust architecture for agentic AI
competitorLandscape.keyContent: Published ZTA guide for agentic AI (May 30, 2026) — treating every agent as untrusted principal that must authenticate, operate in defined boundary, produce auditable records.
competitorLandscape.differentiation: Network-level microsegmentation approach rather than identity-first agent runtime.

competitorLandscape.name: Aembit
competitorLandscape.keyContent: Co-published CSA study finding 68% can't distinguish human from AI activity in logs. Focus on non-human identity management.
competitorLandscape.differentiation: NHI/workload identity focus, not full agent runtime with inference proxy.

industryTrends.marketDemand: Enterprises moving agents from prototype to production face identity security as #1 blocker. The gap between rapid AI prototyping (vibe-coding) and secure production deployment is the central tension.
industryTrends.regulatoryPressure: EU AI Act, emerging AI governance standards requiring traceability, audit trails for agent actions. Compliance review readiness is low — less than half could pass agent-focused audit.
industryTrends.technicalStandards: IETF drafts addressing agent identity (AIMS, WIMSE, Agentic JWT, SCIM for agents). Agent Authorization Profile (AAP) extending OAuth 2.0. SPIFFE/SPIRE for workload identity. MCP/A2A protocol identity bindings emerging.
industryTrends.adoptionBarriers: 68% rate human-in-the-loop as essential but can't implement at scale. 79% can't maintain real-time inventory of active agents. Ownership fragmented across security (39%), IT (32%), AI security functions (13%).

angleForArticle.recommendedNarrative: Frame the guide around the 'agent identity crisis' — enterprises want to put agents in production but can't because identity security is missing. Teleport Beams' LLM Proxy + Delegated Identity offers a production-grade solution. Contrast with ad-hoc approaches (static keys, shared service accounts, borrowed human creds) that dominate today. Position delegated identity as the new 'least privilege for agents' — a runtime property rather than a static config. Include practical architecture: Firecracker VM isolation, per-beam identity certs, inference proxy audit trail.
angleForArticle.targetAudience: Security engineers, platform engineers, and infrastructure leaders evaluating how to safely deploy AI agents in production.
angleForArticle.keyMessage: AI agents need their own identity layer. Teleport Beams provides delegated identity + LLM proxy as the two missing control points for production agentic workloads.
angleForArticle.tl80: Teleport Beams fills the identity gap for production AI agents with LLM Proxy (control what agents are told) and Delegated Identity (control what agents can access), running in ephemeral Firecracker VMs with zero secrets and full audit.
